title: Transient field mapping — campfire notes
content:
Purpose:
These are rough, first-pass notes about handling transient field-like values that show up in scraped or partner-provided datasets.

Context / motivation:
- We keep seeing records with ephemeral fields: session tokens, one-off tracking IDs, preview_url parameters, signed URLs, date-embedded cache-busters (e.g., file_v=20250301).
- These cause labels to vary for otherwise-identical semantic objects and inflate our dedupe / sampling budgets.
- Need a lightweight, reproducible mapping strategy for labeling pipelines (and downstream evals) so that labelers see stable canonical forms and models see less noise.

Constraints and goals:
- Low-work: must be doable by microbatch workers and labelers without heavy infra changes.
- Reversible: mapping should not permanently drop potentially useful signals; we want to preserve raw values in provenance metadata.
- Explainable: heuristics should be documented and easy to audit when a label is surprising.
- Not perfect: prefer conservative normalization that reduces noise but avoids over-normalization (i.e., don't collapse distinct entities).

Brainstormed mapping categories (quick checklist):
- Temporal tokens: sequences that are obviously timestamps, epoch numbers, or calendar dates appended to filenames or query params.
- Fuzzy signature params: e.g., "sig", "s", "token", "auth" in querystring with long base64-like values.
- Tracking keys: utm_*, gclid, fbclid, ga_*, _ga, sessionid-like short alphanumeric.
- Randomized slugs: opt-out-UUIDs and short hashes (8+ hex chars) inside path segments.
- Preview toggles: preview=true/1, nocache flags, v= numeric, cachebust param.
- Provider prefixes that are ephemeral: e.g., cdn-provider.com/signed/..., s3 presigned URLs.

Heuristic proposals (priority order):
1) Query param scrubber (conservative whitelist approach)
   - Default: remove params in blacklist = ["utm_*","gclid","fbclid","_ga","session","sid","s","token","sig","auth","v"]
   - But when param name is ambiguous ("id"), check value pattern: if value matches longbase64/hex/uuid/time then replace with <TOKEN> not drop.
   - Keep numeric versioning if it looks like semantic (e.g., v=2) but remove when long (>6 digits) or looks like epoch.

2) Path slug canonicalizer
   - Replace path segments that match UUID regex or hex-hash regex with <HASH> or <UUID>.
   - Exception: if segment is the last path component and contains a file extension, preserve filename but strip trailing -timestamp or _v### patterns.

3) Signed/s3/presigned detection
   - If host contains known S3/cdn patterns OR URL contains "X-Amz-Signature"/"X-Amz-Expires"/"Signature=", tag as presigned_url and map the whole url to a canonical <SIGNED_URL:provider>.
   - In labeler UI show original value collapsed with a click-to-expand.

4) Short token collapse vs granular keep
   - Short alnum tokens (length <= 6) are likely meaningful keys (region codes, small ids). Keep them.
   - Long tokens (> 20 and base64-like) -> map to <OBFUSCATED_TOKEN>.

Edge examples and proposed outputs (quick):
- https://example.com/image.png?v=20250301 -> https://example.com/image.png?v=<DATE>
- https://foo.com/p/4f5d8a1b/thumb.jpg -> https://foo.com/p/<HASH>/thumb.jpg
- https://cdn.s3.amazonaws.com/bucket/file.png?X-Amz-Signature=abcd... -> <SIGNED_URL:aws-s3>
- https://shop/?utm_source=newsletter&utm_campaign=mar -> https://shop/
- https://svc/preview?token=eyJhbGciOiJI -> https://svc/preview?token=<OBFUSCATED_TOKEN>

Quick regexes (for implementor copy/paste) — keep minimal, approximate:
- UUID: /[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[1-5][0-9a-fA-F]{3}-[89abAB][0-9a-fA-F]{3}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}/
- Hex hash: /\b[0-9a-fA-F]{8,64}\b/ (but guarded by path segment checks)
- Base64-ish: /[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{20,}=*/
- Epoch-ish (seconds): /^(1[5-9]\d{8}|2\d{9})$/  (rough)
- Date in filename: /_(20\d{2})(0[1-9]|1[0-2])(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])|-(20\d{2})(0[1-9]|1[0-2])(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])/

Labeler UI affordances (low-effort):
- Show normalized + original collapsed ("Normalization: path-hash -> <HASH> (view raw)").
- When a field is mapped to a tag (<SIGNED_URL>), labeler can toggle to include raw in context for hard edge cases.
- Add an opt-in checkbox: "consider raw token for label" so rare cases where token is semantically meaningful can be surfaced and flagged.

Sampling / QA plan:
- After heuristics live, run a 10k-sample comparison: labels assigned with raw vs normalized inputs. Focus on precision loss > 1.5%.
- Collect "keep-raw" flags from labelers; if >5% of occurrences for a dataset, iterate mapping rule.

Adjudication checklist (for ambiguous collisions):
- If two records collapse to same canonical form but have different labeled classes, flag for manual review.
- If manual review shows labels should differ, relax normalization (e.g., keep short token).

Open questions / TODOs (campfire-style):
- Should we have dataset-specific rule-sets? Partner feeds often encode meaningful info in tokens (e.g., locale codes). Maybe a per-source allowlist.
- Do we preserve parameter ordering when normalizing? It affects cache-key dedup; probably normalize by sorted keys after scrub.
- How to integrate with provenance store? Minimal: store original raw string + list of applied normalizers + timestamp.
- Can we add lightweight heuristics in client-side SDKs (labeler webapp) to save cycles server-side? Maybe implement JS scrubber mirroring backend regexes.

Notes to self / next steps:
- Build quick Python script that takes sample CSV and outputs normalized column + counts of unique values pre/post. Try it on partner_feed_13.
- Draft small labeler microtask UI mock showing collapse/expand and flag. -> assign to Priya to sketch.
- Add a CI job to detect sudden spike in "<HASH>" occurrences in a dataset (indicates upstream format change).

Quick pseudocode (for backend scrubber):
- parse_url(url)
- for each query param: if key in blacklist -> drop; else if value matches base64/uuid/hex -> value = map_token(value)
- for each path segment: if matches uuid/hash -> replace token; else if filename and date-suffix -> strip suffix to canonical name
- detect presigned by host or params -> map to <SIGNED_URL:provider>
- return canonical_url, list_of_applied_rules, raw_original

Random thought: call this "campfire" because I keep scribbling ideas after 8pm and they are messy. Document will be formalized into a proper playbook if the initial eval is good.

Examples to test with local script (copy/paste-ready):
- "https://app.prod.example.com/checkout?session=4F5A6B&coupon=SPRING"
- "https://cdn.example.com/signed/1234567890abcdef/image.jpg?Signature=XYZ&Expires=167889"
- "https://assets.example.com/img/logo_20241201.png"
- "https://shop.example?utm_source=tw&utm_medium=cpc&orderid=00001234"
- "https://files.svc.com/download/7d8f9a2b3c4d5e6f/report.pdf"

Last note: conservative default is our friend. It's fine to under-normalize and iterate. Keep provenance. Ask labeling leads for one-off exceptions rather than broad rules that might lose signal.

-- Samira
